lines.trans: Good morning again, Madam Carmen! Would you like coffee or black tea?
Black tea without sugar, please, and a slice of warm bread.
Allow me to pour you the freshly squeezed orange juice, madam!
Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: At our inn, five-star service comes naturally... whoops!
Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!
Oh dear! Not a drop on the table, thank goodness... all of it is on my tie!
Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes juice right out.
Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.
Excuse me, madam, I shall retreat to my office with dignity!
The scrambled eggs are delicious, Clara. Tell Rocio my compliments!
I will! Have a lovely morning.

lines.trans: At our inn, five-star service comes naturally... whoops!
Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!
Oh dear! Not a drop on the table, thank goodness... all of it is on my tie!
Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes juice right out.
Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.
Excuse me, madam, I shall retreat to my office with dignity!

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: De nuevo is an idiom meaning 'again'.

examples.trans: It is a new piece.

examples.text: ¡Ah, se abre! Gracias. Soy Clara, la nueva recepcionista.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Clara, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Café solo / negro = black coffee.

examples.trans: It is a black piece.

examples.text: ¡Buenos días de nuevo, señora Carmen! ¿Quiere café o té negro?
examples.trans: Good morning again, Madam Carmen! Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.
He left home without a coat.

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.
We talk about the sugar.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Rebanada de pan tostado = slice of toast.

examples.trans: The slice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las rebanadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the slices from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.
We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

permitir.gloss: to allow; to let (¡Permítame! = Allow me!)

meanings.en: to allow; to let (¡Permítame! = Allow me!)
meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.trans: Will you allow me to look at this map?

examples.text: Esta ventana permite ventilar toda la sala.
examples.trans: This window lets the whole room air out.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sirvo, sirve, sirvió).

examples.text: Servimos desayuno caliente de ocho a diez.
examples.trans: We serve hot breakfast from eight to ten.

examples.text: La encargada sirvió tres tazas de té de menta.
examples.trans: La encargada served three cups of mint tea.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for fruit juice (zumo de naranja).

examples.trans: The juice is here.

examples.text: Vemos los zumos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the juices from the door.

meanings.note: Zumo de naranja = orange juice.

examples.trans: The orange is here.

examples.text: Vemos las naranjas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the oranges from the door.

meanings.note: Pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread; recién salido del horno = fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Tenemos pan recién hecho cada día.
examples.trans: We have freshly baked bread every day.
The juice is freshly squeezed.

meanings.note: Recién exprimido = freshly squeezed.

examples.trans: It is a squeezed piece.

examples.text: ¡Permítame servirle el zumo de naranja recién exprimido, señora!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour you the freshly squeezed orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Muy amable is a warm thank-you ('very kind of you').

examples.trans: It is a kind piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Un vaso de agua = a glass of water.

examples.trans: The drinking glass is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vasos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drinking glasss from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Atención y servicio = guest service.

examples.trans: The service is here.

examples.text: Vemos los servicios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the services from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: De cinco estrellas = five-star.

examples.trans: The star is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estrellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stars from the door.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.
I leave early for the station.

meanings.note: Light exclamation for a small slip or surprise.

examples.text: ¡Uy, casi se me cae la taza!
examples.trans: Oops, I nearly dropped the cup!
Oh my, how late it is already!

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.
We talk about the care.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Glass or ceramic pitcher for water or juice.

examples.trans: The jug is here.

examples.text: Vemos las jarras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jugs from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Also denotes the pouring lip or opening of a jug or tunnel.

examples.trans: The mouth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bocas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mouths from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Opposite of estrecho (narrow).

examples.trans: It is a wide piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuidado, Ernesto, la jarra tiene la boca muy ancha!
examples.trans: Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!

meanings.note: ¡Madre mía! is a mild, warm everyday exclamation across Spain.

examples.trans: The mother is here.

examples.text: Vemos las madres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mothers from the door.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.trans: The drop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las gotas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drops from the door.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Nada mal = not bad at all; menos mal = thank goodness.

examples.text: Nada mal para el primer día.
examples.trans: Not bad at all for the first day.
Thank goodness you brought an umbrella!

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Worn with a collared shirt.

examples.trans: The necktie is here.

examples.text: Vemos las corbatas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neckties from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: ¡No se preocupe! = Do not worry!

examples.text: No te preocupes por el papeleo.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the paperwork.

examples.text: Nos preocupaba el frío de la noche.
examples.trans: We were worried about the night chill.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

gas.gloss: gas; fizz (agua con gas = sparkling water)

meanings.en: gas; fizz (agua con gas = sparkling water)
meanings.note: Agua con gas = sparkling water; agua sin gas = still water.

examples.text: El gas es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The gas is very important here.
We talk about the gas.

quitar.gloss: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)

meanings.en: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)
meanings.note: Quítate el abrigo = take off your coat; quitar el polvo = dust.

examples.text: Quito el polvo del tablero de madera.
examples.trans: I wipe the dust off the wooden board.

examples.text: Quítate el abrigo mojado y pasa.
examples.trans: Take off your wet coat and come in.

meanings.note: Written as one word in modern Spanish.

examples.trans: I will bring breakfast up right away.
I will be right back with the key.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Kitchen or polishing cloth.

examples.trans: The cloth is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cloths from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Retirar los platos = clear the plates.

examples.text: Retiro las tazas vacías de la mesa.
examples.trans: I clear the empty cups from the table.

examples.text: El camarero retiró el plato con cuidado.
examples.trans: The waiter cleared the plate carefully.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Private study or small manager's office.

examples.trans: The office is here.

examples.text: Vemos los despachos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the offices from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -dad.

examples.text: La dignidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dignity is very important here.
We talk about the dignity.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.trans: The egg is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huevos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eggs from the door.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.trans: It is a scrambled piece.

examples.text: Los huevos revueltos están deliciosos, Clara. ¡Felicite a Rocío de mi parte!
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, Clara. Tell Rocio my compliments!

meanings.note: Stronger praise for food and baking.

examples.trans: It is a delicious piece.
they are delicious

meanings.note: Felicitar al cocinero = compliment the chef.

examples.text: Felicito a La panadera por sus bollos.
examples.trans: I compliment The baker on her sweet rolls.

examples.text: Todos felicitaron al equipo el viernes.
examples.trans: Everyone congratulated the team on Friday.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la mejor parte.

examples.trans: The part is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parts from the door.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.
